record.paper_title: Open Problems on Information and Feedback Controlled Systems
record.original_question: How can one formulate the thermodynamics of feedback-controlled systems in a way that explicitly accounts for the thermodynamic consequences of information transfer between the system and the controller, so that quantities such as entropy reduction, extractable work, and efficiency are treated within a consistent thermodynamic framework?

evidence.quote: The second main question is the establishment of the thermodynamics of feedback controlled systems accounting for thermodynamic effects of the information transfer.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Develop a thermodynamic framework for feedback-controlled systems that explicitly incorporates the thermodynamic effects of information transfer between the controlled system and its controller. Specifically:

Setting. Let a physical system $S$ be in contact with one or more heat reservoirs at given temperatures and evolve under a (possibly time-dependent) Hamiltonian or stochastic dynamics. A controller $C$ performs measurements on $S$, obtaining outcomes that are stored in a memory, and uses these outcomes to choose subsequent control protocols applied to $S$ (feedback). Let $I$ denote a suitable information-theoretic quantity (e.g., mutual information, transfer entropy, or related correlation measure) characterizing the information acquired by $C$ about $S$.

Required. Formulate definitions of the entropy production, the heat exchanged with the reservoirs, the extractable work $W_{\mathrm{ext}}$, and the thermodynamic efficiency for the joint process on $S$ together with the measurement and feedback steps, such that:

(i) A generalized second law holds in the form
$$ \langle W_{\mathrm{ext}} \rangle \le -\Delta F + k_B T \, I, $$
or, more generally, an inequality (and an associated equality/fluctuation theorem) bounding entropy reduction in $S$ in terms of $I$ and of the thermodynamic cost of the controller's measurement and memory erasure, consistent with Landauer's principle.

(ii) Equality is attained by an explicitly identifiable class of (quasi-static, reversible, or otherwise optimal) protocols, providing a sharp characterization of the maximal extractable work and of the optimal efficiency for feedback-driven heat engines.

(iii) The framework applies uniformly to classical and quantum, discrete and continuous, single-shot and repeated (continuous-time) feedback, and reduces to the standard second law in the absence of information transfer ($I = 0$).

Provide such a unified formulation, prove the corresponding generalized second law and fluctuation theorem, identify the saturating protocols, and demonstrate the framework on canonical models (e.g., Maxwell-demon-type engines and Langevin systems with continuous feedback).
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: Sagawa–Ueda established a generalized second law and Jarzynski-type equality for feedback-controlled systems, deriving $\langle W_{\mathrm{ext}}\rangle \le -\Delta F + k_B T\, I$ where $I$ is the mutual information acquired by the controller, and a fluctuation theorem with information exchange (PRL 2008, 2012). These results have been extended to continuous feedback, autonomous Maxwell demons, and quantum settings, and a "universal validity of the second law of information thermodynamics" was reported (2024). The general program of a fully unified thermodynamic framework continues to be developed, so the broad question is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Second Law of Thermodynamics with Discrete Quantum Feedback Control
status_evidence.snippet: Sagawa and Ueda derive a thermodynamic inequality giving the maximum extractable work under feedback control in terms of free-energy difference and mutual information.
status_evidence.claim: A generalized second law for feedback-controlled systems involving mutual information has been established.

status_evidence.title: Fluctuation Theorem with Information Exchange
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes a fluctuation theorem in the presence of information exchange between a nonequilibrium system and a feedback controller.
status_evidence.claim: A generalized fluctuation theorem incorporating information exchange has been proved.

status_evidence.title: Universal validity of the second law of information thermodynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work argues for the universal validity of the second law of information thermodynamics.
status_evidence.claim: Recent results extend the information-thermodynamic second law to broad settings.

status_evidence.title: Information Processing and the Second Law of Thermodynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Framework relating information processing to entropy production and bounds on extractable work.
status_evidence.claim: The interplay of information processing and the second law has been formalized.
